title: Welcome & Opening Remarks​: Benchmark Summit 2026 London
gist: Member-only video listing for Adam Panayi's 12:56 welcome and opening remarks at Benchmark Summit 2026 London; no transcript is included. The page's sibling listings sketch the summit agenda: lithium supply, investment and financing, rare earths, the Texas Smackover, Los Azules copper, Chinese OEMs in Europe's EV market and British industrial power costs.

insights.claim: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence's Chief Research Officer Adam Panayi opened Benchmark Summit 2026 London with welcome remarks of about 13 minutes (12:56) on October 23, 2026; the content is members-only.
insights.speaker: Adam Panayi , Chief Research Officer , Benchmark Mineral Intelligence
insights.so_what: Shows who sets Benchmark's research framing for the summit; the substance is behind the member paywall.

insights.claim: The Benchmark Summit 2026 London agenda covered lithium supply and growth, financing for battery, EV and critical minerals projects, rare earths investing, the Texas Smackover lithium play, the Los Azules copper project and the role of Chinese OEMs in Europe's EV market.
insights.speaker: Adam Panayi , Chief Research Officer , Benchmark Mineral Intelligence
insights.so_what: The agenda mix shows which supply-chain stories Benchmark sees as investable now: US lithium brine, copper, rare earths and Chinese competition in European EVs.

insights.claim: One Benchmark Summit 2026 London keynote argued for a faster route to adoption that is profit-led and comes before EVs, under the title 'Winning before EVs: A faster path through profit-led adoption'.
insights.speaker: Adam Panayi , Chief Research Officer , Benchmark Mineral Intelligence
insights.so_what: Suggests electrification adoption may be pitched on profitability rather than mandates, which matters for demand forecasts.
insights.quote: Winning before EVs: A faster path through profit-led adoption

insights.claim: A Benchmark Summit 2026 London keynote introducing 'Regional Power Pavilions' asked whether British industry can stay competitive when one of its biggest costs is also its least predictable.
insights.speaker: Adam Panayi , Chief Research Officer , Benchmark Mineral Intelligence
insights.so_what: Volatile input costs (implicitly power) are being framed as a competitiveness risk for UK industry; watch UK industrial energy policy.
insights.quote: Can British industry remain competitive when one of its biggest costs is its least predictable?
insights.locator: Keynote Presentation: Introducing Regional Power Pavilions

source_meta.author: Adam Panayi , Chief Research Officer , Benchmark Mineral Intelligence
